**How the dialect was implemented:**
- `parse(text) -> dict`, always seeded with root section `""`; keys before any header land there
- Comments only when `#` is literally the first character of a line — indented `#` lines are not comments and fall through to `ValueError`; `#` inside values is text
- Section headers matched as a whole-line `[name]` (empty name rejected); repeated headers merge into the existing section; unrecognizable lines (including `=`-less lines, empty keys, unclosed/malformed headers) raise `ValueError`
- Values split on the *first* `=`; unquoted values strip surrounding whitespace, `key =` yields `""`
- Quoting applies when the (possibly joined) value starts and ends with `"`; inside, only `\"` and `\\` escape, any other backslash stays literal
- Continuation: trailing `\` removed **then** each segment stripped, segments joined with a single space, quoting applied to the joined result — this ordering caught a real bug in my first draft (`1 \` + `2` would have joined to `1  2`)
- Duplicate keys: last wins; non-`str` input: `TypeError` (checked before anything else)
